prompt: A team creates an App Service and, a week later, wants last Tuesday's HTTP logs. They never configured anything. What can they get?
hint: Which signal is kept without being asked?

choices.text: The HTTP logs, from the default workspace
choices.why: There is no default routing; resource logs are discarded without a setting.

choices.text: Platform metrics only
choices.why: Right. Metrics are kept 93 days with nothing configured; the logs are gone.

choices.text: The HTTP logs, if they turn on a setting now
choices.why: A setting routes from now on; nothing earlier can be recovered.

choices.text: Nothing at all, until a workspace exists
choices.why: Metrics exist without any workspace.

prompt: Match each signal to how it reaches a Log Analytics workspace.
hint: One of them needs an agent.

pairs.right: A diagnostic setting on the app
A diagnostic setting on the subscription's activity log
The Azure Monitor Agent and a data collection rule

pairs.left: Platform metrics, to join with logs

prompt: For how many days does Azure Monitor keep platform metrics with nothing configured?
The average of `HttpResponseTime` over a minute is 180 ms. What can you conclude about that minute's customers?
hint: Which minutes give the same average?

choices.text: Each was served in about 180 ms
choices.why: A few four-second requests among fast ones give the same average.

choices.text: Half were faster than 180 ms
choices.why: That is the median, which an average does not give you.

choices.text: Very little about the slow ones
choices.why: Right. The average hides the tail, which is why the shop computes percentiles from logs.

choices.text: That none waited more than 180 ms
choices.why: That would be the maximum, a different aggregation.

prompt: `Http5xx` rises on the shop's App Service plan. What does splitting it by instance tell you that the total does not?
hint: A dimension turns one line into several.

choices.text: Whether one instance produces them all
choices.why: Right. A single bad instance looks like a general problem in the total.

choices.text: Which customer received each error
choices.why: Metrics never identify a request or a customer.

choices.text: The 95th percentile of the errors
choices.why: A count has no percentile, and splitting does not add one.

choices.text: Which line of code threw the exception
choices.why: That is in logs and traces, not in a metric.

prompt: Why does the shop declare the diagnostic setting in Bicep instead of clicking it in the portal?

choices.text: The portal cannot create diagnostic settings
choices.why: It can; the question is where the decision is recorded.

choices.text: Settings created in Bicep are free
choices.why: Ingestion costs the same whoever created the setting.

choices.text: So the decision lives in a reviewed file beside the app
choices.why: Right. A click leaves no record anybody reads.

choices.text: So the logs are kept for 93 days instead of 30
choices.why: Retention is a workspace setting, lesson 9's subject.

prompt: `typo.bicep` routes a category `AppServiceHttpLog` that does not exist, and compiles with exit status 0. Where is it caught?
hint: To Bicep, the category is a string.

choices.text: Nowhere; the setting deploys and routes nothing
choices.why: Resource Manager refuses unknown categories rather than accepting them silently.

choices.text: By the linter, which knows every category
choices.why: The linter raised nothing; categories are not in Bicep's types.

choices.text: At deployment, by Resource Manager
choices.why: Right. Found in the deploy stage, not at build.

choices.text: In the workspace, which drops the table
choices.why: Nothing reaches the workspace from a setting that was refused.

prompt: Setting `logAnalyticsDestinationType` to ___ sends each category to a table of its own instead of AzureDiagnostics.
hint: One word, the value in the shop's file.

prompt: In the shop's rule, what does `transformKql` do to a syslog message about `healthz`?
hint: It runs before the record is stored.

choices.text: Stores it in a cheaper table
choices.why: It filters; nothing is redirected.

choices.text: Drops it before ingestion
choices.why: Right. Rows a transformation drops are never ingested.

choices.text: Masks the word healthz
choices.why: The where clause removes the row; project-away removes a column.

choices.text: Marks it as debug and keeps it
choices.why: Nothing in the transformation sets a level.

prompt: The rule compiles and deploys, and the workspace still receives nothing from the worker VMs. What is the likely missing piece?
hint: A rule names what to collect; what names the machines?

choices.text: A diagnostic setting on each VM
choices.why: Diagnostic settings route platform logs; guest data comes through the agent.

choices.text: The transformation, which drops everything
choices.why: It drops health-check messages only.

choices.text: A Bicep warning that was ignored
choices.why: It compiled with no warning; this is about deployment.

choices.text: An association to each VM, and the agent on it
choices.why: Right. A rule does nothing until associated with machines running the agent.

prompt: Which of these does the shop's data collection rule already leave out? Choose all that apply.
hint: Read the log levels and the transformation.

choices.text: Syslog messages at Info level
choices.why: Yes. Only Warning and above are collected.

choices.text: The HostIP column
choices.why: Yes. project-away removes it before storage.

choices.text: CPU samples between 9:00 and 17:00
choices.why: No. Counters are sampled every 60 seconds, all day.

choices.text: Warnings about health-check requests
choices.why: Yes. The where clause drops them.

prompt: Put the path of a syslog warning from a worker VM to a row in the workspace in order.
items: The VM's system log records the warning
The agent reads it, as the associated rule says
The row is stored, and billed, in the workspace
trap: Putting the transformation after storage is the slip: it runs before, which is why dropped rows cost nothing to keep.

prompt: During an incident, the team needs which customer requests failed between 14:05 and 14:47. Which signal answers that?

choices.text: Platform metrics, split by instance
choices.why: Metrics count requests; they never name one.

choices.text: The activity log
choices.why: It records control-plane operations, not customer requests.

choices.text: Request logs routed to the workspace
choices.why: Right. Logs name each request, if they were routed before the incident.

choices.text: The data collection rule's performance counters
choices.why: Those are CPU and memory from inside VMs.
